title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: In a binary search tree, everything in a node's left subtree is strictly smaller than the node, and everything in its right subtree is strictly larger. Given a binary tree, say whether it is a valid binary search tree. An empty tree is valid.

example.caption: Every node obeys its parent, yet the tree is invalid: 3 sits in the right subtree of 5.

idea.sentence: Send a (low, high) window down the tree. Each node must fall strictly inside it, and each child gets a tighter window.

jargon.plain: A binary tree kept in order: smaller values on the left of a node, bigger values on the right, all the way down.
Equal values are not allowed on either side. A node must be smaller or larger, never the same.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the tree as a level-order list, null for a missing child, e.g. [5,4,6,null,null,3,7]

compare.bruteLabel: Compare each node with every node in its subtrees
compare.optimalLabel: Pass a window down, one check per node
compare.unit: comparisons (a tree that is a long chain)

rows.name: Compare with whole subtrees
rows.note: For each node, scan its left and right subtrees for a value that breaks the rule.

rows.name: Window (low, high)
rows.note: Each node is checked once against two numbers. The stack is as deep as the tree.

fast.takeaway: A node's limits come from all its ancestors, not just its parent. Carry them down as a window and check each node once.

stages.title: Open window
stages.note: The root may be any value, so the window is (minus infinity, infinity).

stages.title: Check the window
stages.note: The node's value must be strictly greater than low and strictly smaller than high. Outside means the tree is invalid.

stages.title: Go left, cap the top
stages.note: Everything on the left must be below this node, so high becomes this node's value. Low stays.

stages.title: Go right, raise the floor
stages.note: Everything on the right must be above this node, so low becomes this node's value. High stays.

edges.title: Empty tree
edges.why: Nothing can break the rule, so an empty tree is valid.

edges.title: Duplicate value
edges.why: The left child must be strictly smaller. An equal value is rejected because the check is value > low and value < high.

edges.title: Grandchild breaks the root
edges.why: 3 is smaller than its parent 6, but it lives on the right of 5. Its window is (5, 6), and 3 is not above 5.

edges.title: Smallest integer value
edges.why: A window made from integer limits would reject this node. Infinity (or no limit at all) accepts it.

gotchas.text: Checking only node.left < node < node.right is the classic mistake. It passes [5,4,6,null,null,3,7] even though 3 is in the right subtree of 5.
Use strict comparisons. Both value <= low and value >= high mean invalid, so duplicates fail on either side.
Use -Infinity and Infinity as the open window. Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER would reject a node holding that exact value, and Number.MIN_VALUE is the smallest positive number, not the lowest.
Do not start with math.MinInt and math.MaxInt as bounds. A node holding that exact value fails the strict test. Use *int bounds where nil means no limit.
&node.Val takes a pointer to the field, not a copy. It is safe here because the bound is only read during the call.

recap.key: Each node must lie strictly between a low and a high handed down from its ancestors.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(h) for the call stack.
moves: check(node, low, high). Null is valid
Reject if node.val <= low or node.val >= high
